title: Courier ETA tracker and its tests
name: Courier ETA tracker

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in these tests that would make them pass or fail nondeterministically? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
In 'subtracts time elapsed since the ping', the fresh ETA is roughly 140 seconds. Why does the test use exact equality with `fresh - 30_000` rather than an approximate comparison?
choices: Because toBe uses approximate comparison for numbers
Because travelMs is identical in both calls and age changes by exactly 30 000 ms, so the rounded result shifts by exactly that integer
Because Math.round always rounds to whole seconds
It is not exact; the test will occasionally be off by 1 ms

questions.prompt: What does ingest() do with a ping whose `at` equals the stored ping's `at`?
choices: Ignores it and keeps the stored ping

questions.prompt: If DeliveryEtaTracker read Date.now() directly instead of the injected clock, which test would be most clearly broken?
choices: 'flags estimates as stale...', since its boundary assertions rely on time advancing by exactly 60 000 and then 1 ms
'forgets an order once it is completed', since delete depends on time
'ignores pings that arrive out of order', since ingest compares against Date.now()
None; the tests only pass timestamps through ping.at
